blocks.title: introduction
blocks.content: The colored Jones polynomial is a one variable polynomial invariant of a knot colored with irreducible finite dimensional representation of $sl(2,\mathbb{C})$ [@Turaev:INVEM88]. The original Jones polynomial [@Jones:link_polynomials] corresponds to the colored Jones polynomial of a knot colored with the irreducible 2-dimensional representation. On the other hand, in [@Cooper/Culler/Gillet/Long/Shalen:INVEM94], D.Cooper, M.Culler, H.Gillet, D.D.Long, and P.R.Shalen introduced a two variable polynomial invariant $A_K(l,m)$ of a knot $K$, called the $A$-polynomial, by using the representations of

blocks.content:
arXiv:math/0401068v1  [math.GT]  8 Jan 2004
THE COLORED JONES POLYNOMIAL AND THE A-POLYNOMIAL
FOR TWIST KNOTS
TOSHIE TAKATA
Abstract. @We show that for a twist knot, the A-polynomial can be obtained from recur-
rences for the summand in Masbaum’s formula of the colored Jones polynomial. Our result
supports the AJ conjecture due to S.Garoufalidis.

blocks.title: Main Theorem
blocks.content: We start with the review of the definition of the $A$-polynomial of a knot $K$ in $S^3$ (see [@Cooper/Culler/Gillet/Long/Shalen:INVEM94] ).
